question: Which side sets the C1 decode step wall: the host (Python launch preparation) or the GPU?
answer: The GPU side. The step wall is invariant to host Python speed, so neither deferring the readback nor making the host faster can reduce it.

method.design: intervention experiment: run the identical child twice, once normally and once under cProfile, which slows host Python without changing GPU work. If the wall is host-bound it must grow; if it is GPU-bound it must not.
method.why_this_works: cProfile inflates Python call cost by a large factor but leaves the GPU kernels untouched, so the two runs differ almost entirely on the host side
method.attribution: each run splits its step wall into the blocking readback inside _read_sample and host time outside it, by wrapping runtime.memcpy and snapshotting per-call-site totals around each step

conclusion.traded_one_for_one: readback + host_outside_readback is conserved across the intervention (35.137 ms unprofiled vs 35.508 ms profiled, both within 0.2% of their own wall), so the two phases are interchangeable and the readback is simply the GPU time the host has not yet covered
conclusion.wall_set_by: the GPU side, at a span of roughly 35 ms per step
conclusion.why_neither_lever_works: deferring the readback recovers nothing because the readback IS the uncovered GPU time; speeding up the host recovers nothing because the wall does not move when host Python changes by 2.2x

recoverable_time_is_the_span_gap.note: the GPU holds the step for ~35 ms while executing only ~17.3 ms of kernels, so about half the span is inter-kernel gap rather than execution

conclusion.redirect: reduce GPU span, not host time: fewer and larger kernels (fusion) or a captured graph replay that removes per-launch gaps. Graph capture already exists on the c8 packed route and the C1 route is eager.

limits: Two points, not a sweep: the intervention varies host Python by 2.22x in one step. A monotonic series would strengthen the invariance claim, though the conservation is already tight to 0.2% in both runs.

cProfile inflates Python cost non-uniformly across functions, so the profiled run identifies that the host side is not binding but does not give a faithful host-side cost ranking. The unprofiled 14.951 ms remains the better estimate of host work.

The ~35 ms GPU span is inferred as wall minus pre-first-launch host time rather than measured from the trace's first-launch and last-finish timestamps; a direct span measurement would confirm the gap figure.
No optimization was attempted. This is a negative result about two candidate levers, not a measurement of any span-reduction alternative.
notes: performance_claim is false and no scoreboard row changed: this redirects an optimization target rather than reporting a speedup.

Supersedes the framing in 2026-09-11-w7900-p5-c1-decode-readback-hideability.json, which established that the readback is not recoverable; this unit establishes that the host is not binding either, leaving the GPU span as the only lever.
